title: Mid-Pleistocene Transition
summary: Between about 1.25 and 0.7 million years ago, Earth's glacial cycles changed from roughly 41,000-year, mostly symmetric cycles to strongly asymmetric cycles of about 100,000 years. A 2019 model study attributes the timing to declining atmospheric CO2 combined with glacial removal of regolith from North America and northern Europe, while a 2021 overview calls the cause unknown.

uncertainty.note: Range follows Willeit et al. (2019), "between ~1.25 and ~0.7 Ma ago"; Eos says "for the past 1.2 million years". The id uses 1000 ka. Years are ka with no 1950 offset.

where.modern_name: Global climate transition; pin at North America (Wikidata point), where regolith removal is modelled
where.historical_name: Earth, Early to Middle Pleistocene; no polities

importance.justification: The change from 41,000-year to ~100,000-year glacial cycles shaped the later Pleistocene ice ages.

reviewer_note: Least sure: Eos says ~120,000-year cycles while Willeit says ~100-ka; the summary uses the latter. The pin has no sourced type site, hence 10000 km. Cause is contested per the sources.
